observation_summary: The StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml method incorrectly handles Unicode characters above U+FFFF (supplementary characters) by treating them as two separate 16-bit surrogate characters instead of a single code point, resulting in incorrect HTML entity encoding.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the iteration logic from using charAt(i) (which only retrieves 16-bit units) to using Character.codePointAt(str, i) (which correctly handles supplementary characters). Additionally, the logic for processing these characters was updated to account for the multi-unit nature of supplementary characters by incrementing the loop index. This is a fundamental change to the computational procedure for processing characters, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_used: The fix replaces 'char c = str.charAt(i);' with 'int c = Character.codePointAt(str, i);'.
The fix adds a conditional check for supplementary characters (c >= 0x010000) and increments the loop index 'i++' to skip the second surrogate unit.
The bug report states that characters represented as 2 characters internally by Java are incorrectly converted.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a conditional check, the core issue is the incorrect algorithmic approach to character iteration and processing, not just a missing guard.
The fix is not about assigning a wrong value, but about changing the entire method of retrieving and processing character data.
